profile_overview.name: Silicon and Stone ICP
profile_overview.one_line_description: Technology policy professionals and decision-makers navigating EU AI regulation, semiconductor supply chains, and digital sovereignty

compliance_clara.example: In-house counsel at a B2B SaaS firm assessing AI Act obligations across product lines
key_concerns: AI Act risk classification for existing products
Cross-jurisdictional compliance (US vs EU divergence)
Documentation and audit trail requirements
Vendor liability and supply chain compliance
compliance_clara.pain_point: Needs to translate dense regulatory text into actionable compliance plans under time pressure, often without dedicated AI governance resources

industrial_ian.example: VP Operations at a German automotive supplier managing semiconductor procurement and AI-assisted production
key_concerns: Semiconductor supply chain concentration risk
US-China decoupling impact on component sourcing
AI adoption in manufacturing under regulatory constraints
Vendor dependency and single-source exposure
content_needs: Supply chain risk mapping and analysis
industrial_ian.pain_point: Caught between pressure to adopt AI for efficiency and uncertainty about regulatory obligations, while managing fragile global supply chains

sovereign_sofia.example: EU Digital Policy Unit analyst tracking AI Act implementation across member states
key_concerns: Digital sovereignty and strategic autonomy
Transatlantic regulatory divergence
Technology standards and governance frameworks
Democratic accountability in AI deployment
sovereign_sofia.pain_point: Difficulty keeping up with rapid regulatory changes across jurisdictions while maintaining analytical rigour and policy relevance

global_citizen.example: Technology journalist or informed professional who follows AI regulation debates and wants analysis beyond headline takes
key_concerns: Understanding real-world impact of AI regulation
Cutting through hype and vendor narratives
Democratic implications of AI governance decisions
Making sense of complex geopolitical technology dynamics
content_needs: Context and background for emerging stories
Clear explanations of technical and legal concepts
Independent perspective free from industry bias
global_citizen.pain_point: Wants substantive analysis but finds most coverage either too superficial (mainstream media) or too captured by industry interests (trade press)

organization_types: US and Canadian startups entering Europe
North American mid-market companies with EU customers
SaaS and AI product companies expanding transatlantically
transatlantic_troy.example: CEO of a US B2B AI startup weighing whether EU market entry is worth the compliance cost, and what the AI Act and cloud certification rules require of a non-EU provider
key_concerns: AI Act obligations for non-EU providers selling into Europe
Data localisation and cross-border transfer requirements
EU cloud certification and sovereignty tier schemes
Public procurement rules favouring European suppliers
content_needs: EU regulatory timelines read from a US vantage point
transatlantic_troy.pain_point: On the outside looking in — must judge whether the European market is worth entering and what the sovereignty landscape will cost to navigate, without an EU legal team on staff

frustrations: AI hype drowning out substantive analysis
Lack of coordinated US-EU resource strategy
Vendor-captured analysis masquerading as independent research
information_sources: Policy briefings and think tank reports
